data.title: The Destruction of Pompeii
sentences: In 79 AD, Mount Vesuvius erupted with a violence that silenced a region and preserved it for eternity.
Years of seismic warnings, including a major earthquake in 62 AD, preceded the catastrophe.
The eruption began with a massive Plinian column of ash and pumice rising thirty kilometers into the sky.
While prevailing winds buried Pompeii under falling lapilli, the city of Herculaneum faced a different fate.
During the night, the eruption column collapsed, triggering superheated pyroclastic surges that swept down the mountain.
These surges killed inhabitants instantly through thermal shock.
Pliny the Elder, commanding the Roman fleet, died attempting a rescue mission at Stabiae.
His nephew, Pliny the Younger, recorded the only surviving eyewitness account of the disaster.
The rapid burial acted as a time capsule, sealing frescoes, organic matter, and victims in ash.
In 1863, Giuseppe Fiorelli developed the technique of plaster casting, revealing the tragic final moments of those trapped in the debris.
